passages.title: The Tall Tower
sentences: Sam, Ana and Ben played a block game at a table.
They stacked blocks to make a tower.
The tower got very tall.
Then Pixel ran under the table to get his ball.
His tail hit a table leg, and the table shook.
The tower fell down.
Everyone laughed.
Then they started a new game.

passages.title: Rain on Match Day
sentences: On Saturday, Ana had a soccer match.
She put on her red shirt and her soccer shoes.
Then it started to rain very hard.
The field got wet and muddy.
The coach moved the match to next Saturday.
Ana frowned and sat down.
Then she played a soccer video game with Ben at home.

passages.title: The Crow and the Pitcher
sentences: It was a hot, dry day, and a crow was very thirsty.
She flew down to a tall pitcher of water.
The water was low, at the very bottom of the pitcher.
Her beak was too short to reach it.
The crow looked around and saw some small stones.
She picked up one stone and dropped it into the pitcher.
The water rose a little bit.
She dropped in more stones, one by one.
Each stone pushed the water higher.
Finally, the water was near the top, and the crow drank it.

credit.title: The Crow and the Pitcher
credit.author: Aesop, retold for Learning to Fly
credit.source: The Aesop for Children (1919), Library of Congress

passages.title: Priya's Rover Stops
sentences: On Thursday, Priya took her rover to the park to test it on the grass.
She drove it in a big circle around a bench.
Then the rover slowed down and stopped in the middle of the path.
The little light on top had turned red.
Priya remembered that a red light means the battery is empty.
She had played with the rover all morning and forgot to charge it.
Priya carried the rover home and plugged it in.
After one hour, the light turned green, and the rover worked again.

passages.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
sentences: A hare liked to tell everyone that he was the fastest animal in the forest.
One day, a tortoise said, "Let's have a race."
The hare laughed, because he was sure he would win.
The animals marked a path from the big oak tree to the river.
When the race began, the hare ran so fast that he was soon far ahead.
He looked back and saw that the tortoise was far behind him.
"I have lots of time," thought the hare, so he lay down under a tree for a nap.
The hare fell asleep, and he slept for a long time.
Meanwhile, the tortoise walked slowly and steadily, one step at a time.
He passed the sleeping hare and kept going.
When the hare woke up, he ran as fast as he could.
But the tortoise had already crossed the finish line by the river.

credit.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
credit.author: Aesop, retold for Learning to Fly
credit.source: The Aesop for Children (1919), Library of Congress

passages.title: The Domino Run
sentences: On Friday after school, Leo and Maya built a domino run in the school library.
It had five hundred dominoes and went around two tables.
Mr. Hill said they could start it at four o'clock so the club could watch.
Ten minutes before four o'clock, a strong wind blew in through an open window.
It pushed a sheet of paper off a desk, and the paper slid into the last domino.
That domino hit the next one, and a long line fell backward.
Maya gasped, and Leo ran to the middle of the line.
He pulled out three dominoes to make a gap, and the line stopped falling at the gap.
Only fifty had fallen.
Maya closed the window, and they set the fallen ones up again.
At four o'clock, the club watched the whole run fall in a perfect line.

passages.title: Leo's Wet Socks
sentences: Leo skated home from the park.
Dark gray clouds filled the sky.
Soon, the streets were wet, and there were puddles everywhere.
Leo got home and took off his shoes.
His socks were very wet.
He put them by the heater to dry.

passages.title: The Empty Plate
sentences: Grandma Rose put a plate of ham sandwiches on the low table in the living room.
Then she went to the kitchen to make some tea.
Sam was upstairs, building a model train track.
Pixel stayed in the living room, next to the sandwiches.
Five minutes later, Grandma Rose came back with the tea.
The plate was empty, and there were crumbs on the rug.
Pixel was licking his nose and wagging his tail.
Sam was still upstairs with his train track.

passages.title: The Bird Bowl
sentences: On Friday evening, Ben filled a bowl with water for the birds.
He put it on the back step.
That night, the weather report said it would be very cold.
In the morning, Ben went out to check the bowl.
The water was hard and cold, and it stayed in the bowl when he tipped it.
A small bird landed on top of it and slid across.
Ben smiled and went inside to get some warm water.

steps.say: The question asks why. A "why" answer tells what made something happen.
First, I find the sentence where the tower falls.
Then I read the sentence just before it, to see what happened first.
Pixel's tail hit a table leg, and the table shook. A shaking table can make a tall tower fall.
So the tower fell because Pixel's tail hit the table and made it shake.
